# Backpressure

Backpressure in a streaming pipeline is the mechanism by which a slow downstream consumer signals an upstream producer to reduce its emission rate, rather than letting an unbounded buffer grow until the process runs out of memory.

## Common Implementations

### Bounded Queues
The producer deposits items into a fixed-size queue. Once the queue reaches capacity, the producer blocks until the consumer drains items, creating back-pressure through synchronous blocking.

### Credit-Based Flow Control
The consumer explicitly grants the producer permission to send N more items. This establishes a quota system where the producer can only emit when it has available credits, and the consumer replenishes credits as it processes items.

### Reactive-Pull Models
Instead of the producer pushing items to the consumer, the consumer requests items on its own schedule. This inverts the control flow, allowing the consumer to pull data at a rate it can handle, inherently preventing buffer overflow.

## Significance

Backpressure is critical for building resilient streaming systems that can handle varying consumption rates without exhausting memory resources. It is especially important in reactive programming frameworks and distributed data pipelines.
